platforms.title: Even the Apostles Called the Resurrection an Idle Tale
platforms.description:
The very first report that Jesus had risen was dismissed as nonsense - by His own apostles. And it came from women, whose word carried almost no weight in that world's courts. No one inventing a resurrection would have opened it there.

"And their words seemed to them as idle tales, and they believed them not... Why seek ye the living among the dead? He is not here, but is risen." (Luke 24:11, 5-6)

The idle tale was true, and it went first to the witnesses the world would not hear. He still sends His word to the overlooked. Stop seeking the living among the dead - the risen Christ is seeking you.

platforms.label: YouTube (Long-form 16:9)
platforms.title: The First Witnesses of the Risen Christ Were Women No Court Would Believe
platforms.description:
When the empty tomb was first reported, the news was not believed. Luke records that the apostles heard it as "idle tales" - nonsense. And the reason cuts deeper than doubt: the report came from women, and in the first-century world a woman's testimony carried almost no weight in a court of law. No one fabricating a resurrection story would ever have chosen those witnesses to open it.

Luke had named these women long before - Mary Magdalene, and Joanna - who followed Jesus from Galilee and supported His ministry from their own means. They watched Him die. They saw where He was buried. At dawn, they were the ones who came back. And so the angels pointed them not to a new idea, but to a promise they had been close enough to hear Him make:

"Why seek ye the living among the dead? He is not here, but is risen: remember how he spake unto you when he was yet in Galilee, Saying, The Son of man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and the third day rise again." (Luke 24:5-7)

The promise had been kept - and the overlooked were the first to know. He still sends His word to those the world will not hear. You need no standing in any court to receive it. Stop seeking the living among the dead; the risen Christ is seeking you.

redteam:
VERDICT: PASS

- youtube_short / facebook description: the quote joins Luke 24:11 ("...idle tales...believed them not") to 24:5-6 ("Why seek ye the living...but is risen") with an ellipsis, though 24:11 falls AFTER 24:5-6 in the chapter. Both fragments are VERBATIM KJV and the citation "(Luke 24:11, 5-6)" discloses the non-contiguous order, so it is honest — but if you want zero appearance of reordering Scripture, quote only the contiguous 24:5-6. Not a KJV-accuracy failure.
- youtube_short / youtube_long: "a woman's word carried almost no weight in that world's courts" is a historical-cultural claim not stated in the verse. It is the standard, defensible apologetic and is softened by "almost," so it passes — but it must stay background color, never presented as doctrine or as a hard historical certainty.
- Titles ("Even the Apostles Called the Resurrection an Idle Tale", "The First Witnesses of the Risen Christ Were Women No Court Would Believe") are curiosity hooks drawn straight from the text (Luke 24:11 "idle tales"; the women as first witnesses). Honest, not clickbait, no doctrinal overclaim.
- CTA "the risen Christ is seeking you" is grace-anchored and truthful to the landing (echoes Luke 19:10). No fear or gain-loss framing anywhere.
- TikTok/Instagram first lines lead with the hook and are punchy; platform tone fits. Hashtags mix broad (#Bible #Jesus) with niche (#EmptyTomb #HeIsRisen) within the per-platform counts.

Minor, optional tightening only; nothing blocks publication.
